category.description: Drawn from the category enum of schemas/mcf-v2/error.schema.json, so one vocabulary describes every error in the product

retryability.description: Drawn from the retryability enum of schemas/mcf-v2/error.schema.json

severity.description: Drawn from the severity enum of schemas/mcf-v2/error.schema.json

mcf_code.description: The MCF-v2 spelling of this error, and it must be a member of the closed code enum in schemas/mcf-v2/error.schema.json. It is null exactly when the error has no MCF counterpart: an error raised and consumed entirely inside the desktop boundary never crosses the protocol, and inventing an MCF spelling for it would extend the protocol's vocabulary to describe something the protocol never carries (AGENTS.md section 7). Null is a statement, not a placeholder - the gate requires every non-null value to resolve in the MCF enum and every value to be unique, because two registry codes sharing one MCF code would make the mapping many-to-one, which this registry does not model.

tauri_code.description: The namespaced spelling reserved for the Tauri transport. The wire currently carries the canonical registry key rather than this value; the divergence is recorded in DEC-055 and is reported by the gate rather than normalized.

meaning.description: What the code means, in one sentence, stated once here rather than re-derived from the name at each call site. Required, because a registered code whose meaning is unstated is a name nothing can act on.
